clue.text: Annoyed head shed tears outside university, being forced into retirement?

parts.note: someone annoyed is put out
the head or top of something

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed around the university's letter
tears that are shed are cast off and scattered, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An irritated boss weeps after leaving the university, pushed out of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a verb with tears, but signals the anagram, as shed things are cast loose.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from retiring an old horse to graze in a field, applied jokingly to people made to stop working.

clue.text: Nurse in a casual shirt as someone at conference?

indicators.note: the nursing word sits inside the shirt phrase

parts.note: a tee is a T-shirt, casual wear
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: Asks whether a nurse wearing a T-shirt is a conference delegate.
explanation.definitionFit: A person present at a meeting or event is one who attends, a participant.

clue.text: Good conductor for one sort of music

definitions.meaning: copper and other such substances carry electricity and heat well

explanation.surface: A fine orchestral maestro, given as an example of a musical style.
explanation.definitionFit: Metallic elements conduct electricity well, and the word is also short for heavy metal rock.

clue.text: Napoleon on a road, where bodies lie

parts.note: Boney was the British nickname for Napoleon Bonaparte

explanation.surface: The French emperor out on a road, near a cemetery.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a graveyard, the place where the dead are buried.

clue.text: Old gold coin deformed, with inscription of South Africa

indicators.note: an inscription is written into something, so the country's code goes inside

parts.note: something deformed is bent
ZA is the international code for South Africa

explanation.surface: A misshapen antique coin stamped with South African lettering.
explanation.definitionFit: A Byzantine gold piece of the Middle Ages, named after Byzantium.

clue.text: School subject, with one of its stories that could be changed for the better

definitions.text: that could be changed for the better

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject
a parable is a story told in religious teaching, such as those of the Gospels

explanation.surface: A religious lesson and one of its tales offering moral improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repairable can be mended, put right or improved.

clue.text: Container at home with one sort of bread

parts.note: a pan is a cooking container
someone at home is in
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tin kept in the house with a type of loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian grilled sandwich bread, often used for toasted sandwiches.

clue.text: Political threat left people hiding upstairs?

parts.note: left-wingers, communists, are reds
a person hiding in a bedroom upstairs might lie beneath the bed

explanation.surface: A political danger from people lurking upstairs in a house.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the hiding place is a whimsical picture rather than a dictionary synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchphrase for the paranoid Cold War fear of hidden communist infiltration everywhere.

clue.text: Mad slogan supporting an EU migrant?

parts.note: fans chant 'up the' before the side they support
a Pole, from Poland, often moved within the EU

explanation.surface: A crazy chant backing a European incomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up the X!' is a supporters' cry, so cheering for a Pole gives the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for crazy or deluded, also meaning in a hopeless mess.

clue.text: Little energy, no longer alive? Cheer up!

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy, a little bit of the word
the late someone has died

explanation.surface: Low on energy and dead, then told to brighten up.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift spirits, make someone joyful.

clue.text: Cockney optimist had to work

indicators.note: Cockney speakers drop the initial H

parts.note: an optimist is one who hopes, a hoper
had a meal means ate

explanation.surface: An upbeat Londoner had to get a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Functioning, running or acting as a machine or person does.

clue.text: A children's fantasy land's not right — one lies

indicators.note: 'not' asks for the letter standing for right to be absent from the fantasy land

parts.note: Narnia is the land of C S Lewis's children's books, here with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A magical realm from children's books is missing its right-hand part.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical figure struck dead for lying, so a byword for a liar.

clue.text: Heading on organiser's list creates a stir

definitions.meaning: a list of tasks is headed '...'

explanation.surface: A title on someone's planner causes a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a task-list title and a noun for a fuss or commotion.

clue.text: Actors taking part? It leads to voices being raised

definitions.text: It leads to voices being raised

parts.note: the cast of a play are its actors
a share or portion, a ration

explanation.surface: Performers getting a role, and something that causes shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'voices being raised' looks like anger, but means the high voices of castrati.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelding boys before puberty kept their singing high, as with the castrati.

clue.text: One who offers praise, waving team's icon

indicators.note: a waving flag moves about, so the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A fan cheering as the club's hero flutters on a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: An encomium is a speech of high praise; its author is the eulogist.

clue.text: Old wolf, maybe, grabs tail of one nymph

indicators.note: the old wolf takes hold of the letter inside

parts.note: a wolf is one example of a canid, the dog family

indicators.note: the last letter of the word one

explanation.surface: An aged wolf seizes a creature by its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a sea nymph, daughter of the Titan Oceanus.

clue.text: Trojan, say, breaking law, needing horse to get around

indicators.note: the horse word goes around the scrambled letters

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: law broken gets its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A Trojan breaking the law and needing a horse to get about, recalling Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trojan' suggests the wooden horse of Troy, but here it is the computer kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trojan is a type of harmful computer program disguised as something benign.

clue.text: Buzz rising around one thoroughfare and another that is much desired

indicators.note: the buzz word goes around the street abbreviation
in a down clue the word goes upwards, so reads backwards

parts.note: a hum is a buzzing noise
ST is street
AVE is avenue, another thoroughfare

explanation.surface: A buzz of excitement on one street and another, for something coveted.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads the buzz word from the bottom up, giving MUH.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes something essential or highly sought after, an item everyone wants.

clue.text: An aged garment that doesn't need exposure to air

definitions.text: that doesn't need exposure to air

parts.note: AE abbreviates Latin aetatis, aged
a robe is a garment

explanation.surface: An old piece of clothing that needn't be aired.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism that lives without oxygen, so does not need air.

clue.text: It's about two countries sharing oil out

indicators.note: letters put out of order are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two nations dividing up an oil supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to both England or Britain and Ireland together.

clue.text: Gorge a small measure? Some diners can't cope with it at all

definitions.text: Some diners can't cope with it at all

parts.note: to gorge is to glut, overeat
an en is a printer's small unit of width

explanation.surface: Stuff yourself with a small portion, though some eaters can't manage it.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheat protein that coeliacs and others with intolerance must avoid.

clue.text: Looking cross about revolutionary newspaper's view

indicators.note: the angry colour goes round the reversed paper

parts.note: red in the face from anger

indicators.note: turned round, the word reads backwards

parts.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper; 's is is

explanation.surface: An angry reader frowns over a radical paper's opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To view something as a particular thing is to regard or consider it so.

clue.text: Designation of Sir Lionel?

parts.note: A baronet styled Sir has this abbreviated title after his name

explanation.surface: Asks what title a knight called Lionel bears.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation for baronet, and the surname of Oliver! songwriter Lionel.

clue.text: Space traveller has to hit hard with limited power

indicators.note: the hit word limits, or encloses, the power letter

parts.note: to sock is to punch
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: An astronaut must strike forcefully despite little strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Spock is the Vulcan officer of Star Trek's starship crew.

clue.text: Moved out with group on the road?

indicators.note: the word out is moved around

parts.note: a ring is a gang or group

explanation.surface: Went out with the band on tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bands touring travel from place to place performing; idiomatically on the road.

clue.text: The rope tangled in the shrub

indicators.note: a tangled rope has its letters knotted into another order

explanation.surface: A rope snarled in a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American bush whose bitter fruit was used in place of hops.

clue.text: From the sound, interprets certain musical instruments

indicators.note: the synonym is said aloud, matching another word

parts.note: to interpret is to read

explanation.surface: An interpreter of some instruments by ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodwinds like oboes and clarinets are reed instruments.

clue.text: Turning over message not cast in stone?

parts.note: rev, a revolution, is a turn
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a cable is a telegram

explanation.surface: Reversing a note that isn't carved in stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to be withdrawn or cancelled, so not permanent.
